evals.prompt: I just joined a new team and was handed a Python repo at ./svc-billing. Generate a newcomer quickstart page so I can ramp up.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./svc-billing --out docs/reports/quickstart. Walks the scope, detects Python + (likely Django/Flask), identifies entry points + tests + docs, builds all 7 sections, emits index.html + README.md, reports composite score and per-section verdicts.
expectations: The response invokes /rui-report-quickstart create with --scope
The response identifies the language and framework from the scope
The response describes the 7-section payload (overview, concepts, directory-map, onboarding-flow, commands, faq, further-reading)
The response mentions both outputs: index.html AND README.md
The response reports a composite score and per-section verdicts

evals.prompt: I need a quickstart for our open-source repo at /Users/me/projects/cli-tool. The page should be HTML and a markdown mirror so the community can fork and edit.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope /Users/me/projects/cli-tool. Two outputs: index.html (browser-viewable, Vue 3) and README.md (hand-editable knowledge base). Both contain the same 7 sections in canonical order with identical ## headers.
expectations: The response invokes /rui-report-quickstart create with the absolute scope path
The response mentions both index.html AND README.md as outputs
The response notes that the markdown mirror uses identical ## headers to the HTML page
The response explains why the mirror is useful (easy to copy, edit, and publish in static sites)

evals.prompt: I want to onboard new hires onto our internal monorepo at ~/work/monorepo. Generate a quickstart — I want the page to be Chinese since most of my team reads Chinese.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ~/work/monorepo --language zh. All 7 sections emit Chinese content. Tone is localized, but framework names, file paths, and command names remain in their original language. Section structure stays canonical.
expectations: The response uses --language zh
The response notes that all 7 sections are emitted in Chinese
The response keeps the canonical section structure (no reordering)
The response mentions that technical terms (e.g. framework names, command names) remain in their original language

evals.prompt: Run a quickstart on ./legacy-app — it's an old Java app with no README, no CONTRIBUTING, no docs folder. Just a src/ tree and a pom.xml.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./legacy-app. All 7 sections render with # TODO markers where evidence is missing (faq, further-reading will be TODO-heavy). Composite score will be low (likely D or F). The page is still generated — better a # TODO page than no page.
expectations: The response does NOT abort despite missing README/CONTRIBUTING/docs
The response renders all 7 sections with # TODO markers for missing facets
The response notes that faq and further-reading will be TODO-heavy
The response computes a low composite score (D or F) and surfaces it in the header
The response emphasizes the no-fabrication rule: missing data renders as TODO, not invented prose

evals.prompt: I want to skip the markdown mirror — just give me the HTML page this time. Can I do that?
evals.expected_output: Yes, use --no-mirror. Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope <path> --no-mirror. Only index.html is written; README.md is skipped. Useful when the markdown mirror would clutter the repo (e.g. embedded widgets, interactive demos).
expectations: The response confirms --no-mirror is supported
The response explains the use case (HTML-only when mirror would clutter)
The response shows the full command line including --no-mirror

evals.prompt: Generate a quickstart for ./my-app but I want the directory map to go 4 levels deep instead of the default 3.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./my-app --depth 4. The directory-map section annotates the top 4 levels (vs default 3). Other 6 sections unchanged.
expectations: The response uses --depth 4
The response notes that only the directory-map section is affected
The response explains the trade-off (deeper maps are more informative but noisier)

evals.prompt: Why does the report have a composite score and per-section verdicts? What's the grading scale?
evals.expected_output: The report is a self-assessment of how well the project teaches a newcomer. Per-section verdict is pass (≥0.90, ✅), partial (0.50–0.89, ⚠️), or fail (<0.50, 🚫). Composite = mean(coverage) × 100. Grade: A≥90, B≥75, C≥60, D≥40, F<40. Low scores surface a call-to-action: 'fill the # TODO markers to improve your onboarding'.
expectations: The response explains the per-section verdict thresholds (pass / partial / fail)
The response explains the composite score formula (mean × 100)
The response lists the grade scale (A / B / C / D / F)
The response frames the score as a self-assessment of onboarding quality, not code quality

evals.prompt: I notice the page has a sidebar with reading-progress, sidebar, topbar, etc. — does this quickstart use the same 9-region layout as docs/quickstart/?
evals.expected_output: No. rui-report-quickstart does NOT use the docs/quickstart/ 9-region layout. Its primary contract is the newcomer-facing 7-section onboarding report; implementation may be direct HTML or a reusable multi-file scaffold when available. The two skills are complementary, not overlapping: rui-docs-quickstart is a maintainer manual, while rui-report-quickstart generates a newcomer-facing guide for any local project.
expectations: The response clarifies that rui-report-quickstart does not use the docs/quickstart/ 9-region layout
The response explains that the primary contract is the 7-section onboarding report rather than a specific internal file split
The response distinguishes the two skills: rui-docs-quickstart is a maintainer manual; rui-report-quickstart is a newcomer-facing page generator

evals.prompt: I ran a quickstart yesterday and edited README.md to add a FAQ entry. Today I re-ran. Will my edit survive?
evals.expected_output: By default, no — regenerated outputs overwrite the previous README.md body. If the runtime can detect obvious manual edits, it should warn before replacement, but merge behavior is not guaranteed. As a workaround, keep custom additions in a separate file and merge them back after the run.
expectations: The response acknowledges that re-running overwrites the markdown mirror body
The response notes that section headers are byte-stable, so a re-run produces a structurally compatible file
The response suggests a workaround (separate file, manual merge, or analyzer dirty-check)

evals.prompt: I'm worried the analyzer will hallucinate — what stops it from inventing file paths that aren't in my repo?
evals.expected_output: The no-fabrication rule (Rule 9 in SKILL.md) explicitly forbids inventing file paths. Every claim in the 7 sections must cite a real file/line/symbol from the scope or render as # TODO. The page has a 'TODO badge' UI for TODO markers; the mirror has a '# TODO' header. Verdicts drop for any section that has TODO markers. The composite score reflects this — high TODO count = low score = call-to-action to fill them in.
expectations: The response cites the no-fabrication rule explicitly
The response explains the # TODO marker convention in both the HTML page and the markdown mirror
The response notes that verdicts and the composite score penalize heavy TODO use
The response frames the score as a self-audit mechanism

evals.prompt: What 7 sections does the quickstart cover and in what order?
evals.expected_output: Canonical 7 sections in this order: 1) Project Overview (overview), 2) Key Concepts (concepts), 3) Directory Map (directory-map), 4) Onboarding Flow (onboarding-flow), 5) Command Cheatsheet (commands), 6) FAQ (faq), 7) Further Reading (further-reading). The order is fixed; the page does no reordering. Section slugs are the canonical identifiers used in data.js and the markdown mirror's ## headers.
expectations: The response lists all 7 sections by name and slug
The response preserves the canonical order (overview → concepts → directory-map → onboarding-flow → commands → faq → further-reading)
The response notes that the order is fixed and not subject to reordering

evals.prompt: What's the difference between rui-report-quickstart, rui-report-files, rui-report-diagram, and rui-report-test?
evals.expected_output: They are complementary report skills with different outputs: rui-report-files analyzes file size and coupling, rui-report-diagram produces architecture diagrams, rui-report-test generates a six-scene repo health report, and rui-report-quickstart creates a seven-section newcomer quickstart. The first three often ship with reusable modular report scaffolds; quickstart's primary contract is the onboarding output itself, whether emitted directly or via reusable scaffolds.
expectations: The response notes that quickstart is defined primarily by its 7-section onboarding contract, not by a required internal file split
The response distinguishes each skill by its output (size report / diagram / test / quickstart)
The response clarifies that the 4 are complementary
